chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Fazzal, from Ibrahim ibn Usman, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I said to him, 'A man owes me some dirhams, and his house was a mortgage (pledge), so I intended to sell it.' He said, 'I seek Refuge for you with Allah that you would remove the shade from his head.'

key_terms.أُعِيذُكَ بِاللَّهِ: I seek Refuge for you with Allah (a phrase of advice/exhortation)
key_terms.ظِلِّ رَأْسِهِ: The shade of his head (metaphor for shelter/comfort)

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on selling a debtor's house if it is used as collateral for a debt?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) advises against selling a debtor's mortgaged home to recover a debt, using the metaphor of 'removing the shade from his head' to emphasize preserving the debtor's shelter and dignity. This ruling highlights the Shia legal principle of *ihsan* (benevolence) in financial transactions, prioritizing the debtor's comfort over strict creditor rights. It reflects the broader Islamic ethic of leniency in debt collection, encouraging creditors to act as benefactors rather than mere enforcers.
